problem: Multi-robot data for vision-based navigation is hard to exploit because platforms differ in dynamics. Conventional hierarchical policies (high-level waypoints plus low-level tracker) let the perception level command waypoints the deployment robot cannot physically achieve.
motivation: Collecting large, diverse datasets on a single robot is expensive (e.g., drones with battery limits), yet visual knowledge of obstacles transfers across platforms. Dynamics must be handled per robot, without blocking sharing of perception data.
key_idea: Train a shared, dynamics-agnostic perception model (image + pose changes -> collision rewards) on heterogeneous robot data and a robot-specific dynamics model (actions -> pose changes), then chain them into one integrated model for MPC planning at test time.
insight: Because the dynamics model's output (kinematic pose changes) is the perception model's input, the two compose with no retraining, so the planner only evaluates dynamically feasible trajectories. Comparison to conventional hierarchy shows the gain appears only when the deployment dynamics differ from the perception data (limited-steering Jackal 0% -> 100%, high-speed drone 20% -> 100%, sim right-turn-only 0% -> 56%), while on the normal platform both match. Adding data from other platforms (human video in the industrial environment) raised success from 33% to 87%.
method: Perception model: neural net f(o_t, p_{t:t+H}) -> predicted collision rewards, trained with an L2 loss on pooled data from Kobuki, Jackal and hand-held camera; needs only images, pose deltas and rewards
Dynamics model: neural net f(s_t, a_{t:t+H}) -> pose changes (x, y, yaw), trained only on a small reward-free dataset from the deployment robot
Integrated model: composition f_perc(o, f_dyn(s, a)) yields rewards from actions without extra training
Planning: MPC that maximizes a task reward (collision + goal-angle + action-magnitude terms) using CEM (sim) or MPPI (real robots), executing the first action and replanning at 4-6 Hz
Data balancing: collision-data rebalancing (50:50) and environment rebalancing during multi-source perception training

setting.backbone: Small CNN/MLP perception and dynamics networks (trained from scratch), planned with CEM/MPPI
setting.training_data: Perception: Kobuki office 32,884 pts/3.7h, Jackal urban 50,000 pts/3.5h, GoPro human industrial 12,523 pts/1.2h; sim car 500k pts. Dynamics: Jackal 50k pts, Bebop drone 4,977 pts, sim variants 5k pts each
setting.observation: Monocular RGB 54x96 (two stacked frames in sim), GPS goal for Jackal
setting.action_space: Continuous linear/angular velocity (Jackal), angular velocity (drone, sim car)
setting.privileged: none (GPS goal coordinate given for the Jackal task)

numbers.extra: perception trained on 3 platforms; Jackal deployment
perception trained on 3 platforms; Jackal has no own data in this environment

numbers.evidence: Table: Right turn only 56% (baseline 0%); Limited steering 84% vs 68%; lag 40% vs 0%; normal 96% both

numbers_note: No standard benchmarks; results are small-scale real-world/sim success rates from figures/tables.
results: HInt beats single-source variants (Urban 100% vs 13% Jackal-only; Industrial 87% vs 33% without human data). Against conventional hierarchy it matches on normal dynamics but wins strongly on altered dynamics (e.g., 100% vs 0% limited-steering Jackal, 100% vs 20% high-speed drone).
limitations: Generalizes only within the training distribution (similar cameras/ground robots), not e.g. to legged robots
Zeroth-order sampling planner limits to short-horizon navigation; small trial counts (5-15 per condition)
